question: six checkpoints are three architecture families; what does the arm effect look like when the clustering is modelled instead of apologised for
population_note: 3420 -> 1559 rows before the k>=6 cut; src/common/population.py, panel() defaults

mixedlm.note: with three families the family-varying arm slope is barely identified and REML shrinks it hard, so this Wald interval is narrower than the between-family spread alone would license; the clustered, family-t and bootstrap intervals below are the widths to quote

bayes.model: binomial likelihood, logit scale; control level and arm gap each carry a family offset and a checkpoint offset nested in it

verdict: arm effect 76.4 pts; the least favourable of six frequentist intervals has lower bound 63.2 pts; the posterior predictive gap for an architecture family outside the panel is 65.3 pts [5.9, 93.3] with P(gap>0)=0.996; the exact-rate gap ranges 34.4 to 86.4 pts across 210 specifications and keeps its sign in 100% of them.
